title: Joints, cartilage, arthropathy and soft tissue

steps.tx: Shoulder magnetic resonance imaging provides definitive assessment of the myotendinous cuff. **Rotator cuff tears** most frequently involve the **supraspinatus tendon** near its footprint insertion on the greater tuberosity, with full-thickness tears demonstrating fluid signal traversing from articular to bursal surfaces on T2-weighted fat-suppressed sequences.

steps.tx: Magnetic resonance criteria differentiate internal fibrocartilaginous derangements of the knee. Knee **meniscal tear** diagnosis requires hyperintense fluid or linear intrameniscal signal unambiguously contacting an articular surface (superior, inferior, or free margin) on at least two consecutive slices, known as the **two-slice touch rule**, separating genuine tears from internal mucoid degeneration.

steps.tx: Knee cruciate ligament trauma displays direct and secondary biomechanical indicators. **Anterior cruciate ligament** rupture presents with primary discontinuity, non-visualization, or abnormal horizontal orientation of fibers, accompanied by characteristic secondary signs including bone contusions in the **lateral femoral condyle** sulcus and posterior lateral tibial plateau.

steps.tx: Cross-sectional arthrography defines pathology of the superior glenoid labrum. **SLAP tear** (superior labrum anterior-to-posterior) involves the anchor of the long head of the **biceps tendon**, distinguished from a normal sublabral sulcus on MR arthrography by lateral extension into the labral substance, width > 2 mm, or posterior extension.

steps.tx: Plain radiographic changes establish diagnostic patterns across chronic arthropathies. **Rheumatoid arthritis** demonstrates bilateral symmetric marginal erosions, uniform joint space narrowing, periarticular osteopenia, and synovial pannus formation, characteristically targeting the **MCP joints** (especially 2nd and 3rd), PIP joints, and carpus while sparing DIP joints.

Rheumatoid arthritis demonstrates bilateral symmetric marginal erosions, uniform joint space narrowing, periarticular osteopenia, and synovial pannus formation, characteristically targeting the MCP joints especially 2nd and 3rd, PIP joints, and carpus while sparing DIP joints.

rows: MCP and PIP joints; spares DIP

steps.tx: Microcrystalline inflammatory arthropathies display distinctive osseous remodelling signs on diagnostic radiographs. **Gouty arthritis** typically demonstrates well-defined, punched-out periarticular erosions with sclerotic borders and **overhanging cortical edges** (Martel sign), preserving joint space and bone mineralization until late stages, alongside hyperdense soft-tissue tophi.

steps.tx: Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate crystal disease produces pathognomonic chondrocalcinosis in articular fibrocartilage across major peripheral joints. **CPPD arthropathy** manifests as linear or punctate calcification of hyaline cartilage and fibrocartilage (**chondrocalcinosis**), prominently affecting the knee menisci, wrist triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC), and pubic symphysis.

steps.tx: Focal subchondral ischemic events lead to fragment instability in adolescents and young adults. **Osteochondritis dissecans** (OCD) characteristically affects the non-weightbearing lateral aspect of the **medial femoral condyle** (75%), where high T2 signal fluid rim demarcating the progeny bone fragment on MRI indicates mechanical instability requiring surgical fixation.
